assessment.title: CARSI Mould Remediation Practitioner — Practical task: plan and evidence a medium mould job
assessment.instructions:
## Practical task

**Prerequisite: CARSI Level 2 Mould Remediation completed.** This task assesses whether you can apply Level 2 to a whole job; it is one of the two requirements for the CARSI Mould Remediation Practitioner designation (the other is the final designation exam at 80%).

Plan and document a medium mould remediation job from first visit to verified handover. Use a real job you have attended, or the supplied job: a single-storey brick-veneer home in Wollongong, built in 1984, where a leaking shower recess has fed mould into the shared wall with the main bedroom. Visible growth covers the bedroom wall base (2.8 m long, 0.6 m high) and the back of the built-in wardrobe (1.0 m by 0.5 m). The bedroom is 3.4 m by 3.2 m with a 2.4 m ceiling. On arrival the bedroom air reads 23 degrees C and 72 %RH. A 10 A GPO in the bedroom shares a circuit with the hallway. The occupants include a child with severe asthma.

Submit one PDF, or a set of photos and documents, containing:

1. **Site reading and size.** A sketch with every patch measured, the total visible growth in square metres and the size band it falls in (WorkSafe Queensland scale), the smell and photos numbered to the sketch, and the occupants recorded. For each area (bedroom, wardrobe, ensuite, hallway), record what you see, measure, how it connects and what you smell, and the decision you made using the condition terms from Level 2, with your reasons. State what makes this job more than a wipe-down.
2. **Cause and moisture map.** The moisture source found and how it will be fixed, a moisture map starting from a dry reference in an unaffected area of the same material, the instrument and mode used for each reading, and the air logged in degrees C, %RH, g/kg and dew point. Note the asbestos check you would arrange before cutting, given the year of construction.
3. **Containment, engineering controls and power.** The containment layout (sheeting, entry and decontamination area, sealed vents, access control and waste route), the containment volume in cubic metres, the air scrubber's delivered airflow and the resulting air changes per hour, and how you will confirm negative pressure. The target pressure difference and air-change figure are set by your supervisor against the licensed standard; state the figures you were given. Include a 230 V power budget totalling each machine's current per circuit, on an RCD, with inspected, tested and tagged leads.
4. **PPE and people.** The PPE set for each worker (respirator type marked AS/NZS 1716, fit-test date, fit check, skin and eye protection), the heat plan, and how the child with severe asthma and other occupants are kept away from the work area and its exhaust. Refer any health question to a GP; give no medical advice.
5. **Order of work, drying and verification.** The steps in order, from fixing the water to rebuild; the material removed in square metres and the waste bags and route; the drying plan applying the airflow rule (contain and remove before blowing air, dehumidify inside the containment) with a dehumidifier g/kg check; and the four verification checks (cause fixed, visibly clean, dry to the reference, normal air) completed before the containment comes down, with the tolerance your supervisor set.
6. **Job file and communication.** The job file contents as built during the work, a scope-change note with written approval, the price in AUD with GST shown, the plain-English handover given to the occupants, including what they must do to stop the mould returning, and a short note to the owner's insurer separating the cause, the extent in square metres and the evidence plan from opinion.

Use Australian English, metric units and 230 V equipment throughout. Name standards only; do not copy or paraphrase text from any standard.

criteria.label: Site reading, size and cause
criteria.description: Every patch measured and totalled in square metres with the correct size band; each area decided on recorded evidence with reasons, taking the cautious call where evidence is mixed; moisture source identified with a fix; moisture map from a dry reference with instrument and mode recorded; air logged in degrees C, %RH, g/kg and dew point; asbestos check arranged for a pre-1990 building before any cutting.

criteria.label: Containment, engineering controls and 230 V power
criteria.description: Containment matched to a medium job with sealed sheeting, entry and decontamination area, sealed vents, access control and waste route; volume and air changes per hour calculated correctly; negative pressure confirmed against the supervisor-set target; power budget totalled per circuit at 230 V on an RCD with tested and tagged leads.

criteria.label: PPE, people and health boundaries
criteria.description: P2-or-higher respirator marked AS/NZS 1716, fit-tested before first use and fit-checked each wear; higher-risk skin and eye protection inside containment; heat plan stated; the child with severe asthma and other occupants kept away from the work and exhaust; health questions referred to a GP with no medical advice given.

criteria.label: Order of work, airflow rule and verification
criteria.description: Steps in the correct order from fixing the water to rebuild; porous materials wet over 48 hours or with visible growth removed and quantified; waste wrapped, sealed and routed; no air blown across growth before containment and removal; dehumidifier proven with a g/kg drop; all four verification checks completed before the containment comes down.

criteria.label: Job file, communication and Australian production
criteria.description: Job file built as the work happens with readings and photos; scope change recorded and approved in writing; price in AUD with 10% GST shown; plain-English handover with prevention advice; insurer note separates fact from opinion; Australian English, metric units and 230 V throughout; standards named only, with no copied or paraphrased standard text.
